clue.text: Publishers engaged in fraud making slip

indicators.note: something engaged in another piece is held inside it, so the publishers sit within the fraud

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle
OUP is Oxford University Press, a well-known publisher

explanation.surface: A publishing house caught up in a swindle makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' looks like an error but means a small piece of paper; 'engaged in' puts the publishers inside the fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher is a small paper slip handed in for a discount.

clue.text: I book to get into pool, showing natural desire

indicators.note: to get into a place is to go inside it, so these letters are placed within the pool

parts.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool

explanation.surface: Someone takes a book to the swimming pool, revealing a natural urge.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is an outdoor public swimming pool, common in Britain. IB goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is the instinctive sexual drive, a natural appetite or urge.

clue.text: Christian basilica put up food in historic city

parts.note: Saint Peter's in Rome is the great Christian basilica

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: Someone builds a church and serves food in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like building the basilica but turns GRUB upside down to make BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city founded by Peter the Great in 1703 has a long, eventful past, so historic fits.

clue.text: Speak aggressively in French of allegation

parts.note: de is the French word meaning of
a claim is an assertion or allegation

explanation.surface: Someone attacks verbally in French about an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to orate vehemently, speaking forcefully and with rhetorical passion.

clue.text: Intricate hassle having to alter unrealistic plans

indicators.note: to alter something is to change it, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complicated hassle forces a change to impractical schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes daydreams or schemes with no chance of coming true.

clue.text: Artist making final move on board grabbing bottle

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it, so one piece clasps the other inside

parts.note: mate (checkmate) is the move that ends a chess game
bottle is British slang for courage, and grit is courage too

explanation.surface: A chess player makes the winning move while seizing a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for nerve or courage, here GRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rene Magritte was the Belgian surrealist painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Sour hand misbehaving in country

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not keep their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy farmhand behaves badly somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a republic in Central America, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Put forward comment about ministry, centre of affairs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the comment wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a note is a brief comment or remark
Min is the usual abbreviation for ministry

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here of the word affairs

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a remark about a government ministry and its central business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the comment round the ministry plus the centre of 'affairs', which is its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to propose them as a candidate.

clue.text: Belligerent female extended flower

definitions.meaning: a warlike, fierce woman, after the warrior women of Greek myth
a very long river; a flower is crossword code for something that flows

explanation.surface: A combative woman and a long-stemmed bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but something that flows, a river; the South American river is famously long.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical warrior women gave their name to aggressive, strong women, and the river is among the world's longest.

clue.text: Some antisocial characters heading west somewhere in Greece

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left, backwards
some of the characters means only part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Some unfriendly types travel west to a place in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: SOC sits inside 'antisocial' and is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kos (also spelt Cos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese, so a place in Greece.

clue.text: Work a lot in being trained? It's not mandatory

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music

indicators.note: being trained means being shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lot of work goes into training, but it is voluntary.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is followed by TIONAL, the rearranged letters of 'a lot in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is voluntary, a matter of choice rather than requirement.

clue.text: One puncturing plumbing, maybe delivering angry speech

indicators.note: something puncturing another goes into it, so this letter is put inside

parts.note: plumbing is an example of a trade, signalled by maybe
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A burst pipe has someone ranting furiously at the plumber.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, furious outburst of criticism.

clue.text: Derogatory lie countryman concocted about politician

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the politician
concocted means made up or cooked up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A rural man invents a lie about a politician, and it is not flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'lie countryman' are rearranged around MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory remark is disparaging, the opposite of flattering praise.

clue.text: Subdue animal

definitions.meaning: to intimidate or browbeat into submission

explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, and the farm beast is an obvious animal.

clue.text: Obstructs rowers' benches

definitions.meaning: the cross-seats on which oarsmen sit in a boat

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means foils or frustrates; the noun names the crosswise seats in a rowing boat.

clue.text: Queen, say, starts off every duty held in admiration

parts.note: in card games the queen is one of the honour cards, so say marks it as an example

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, here of every and duty

explanation.surface: The monarch begins each day's duties to admiring subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace, king, queen, jack and ten are 'honours' in bridge; add E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honoured is respected and esteemed.

clue.text: Like runners and jumpers, half of them allowed in capital clubs

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the outer pieces

parts.note: capital means excellent, as does A1, written AI with the 1 as I

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters, here of them

parts.note: to let is to allow
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Half the athletes are allowed into city sports clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means first-rate, A1, written with I for the one; 'in' puts the rest inside it and the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes who run and jump are sporty and fit, so an athletic build suits them.

clue.text: Excellent ship backed by energy and skill

indicators.note: backed by means followed by, so the energy comes after

parts.note: fine means excellent or very good
SS stands for steamship
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fine vessel, powered by energy and skilfully handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' might suggest reversal, but SS reads the same both ways; it means followed by.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate, refined skill in handling a situation.

clue.text: Deep regard, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: to regard is to look at or see

explanation.surface: A profound look, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep' looks like an adjective but is the noun: the deep is the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic term for the ocean.

clue.text: Bookworm, for instance, supported by good authoritative teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue being supported by means sitting above, so the other pieces follow

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance
the head is the head teacher, the one in charge of a school

explanation.surface: A studious pupil is backed by a good, commanding teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is a studious, intellectual type, an informal synonym for an intellectual.

clue.text: Following a correct course like a disciplined athlete?

definitions.meaning: a well-drilled runner stays on the correct running lane, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means proceeding correctly; read literally it is a runner sticking to the proper circuit.

clue.text: Tell where a warring couple might go?

definitions.text: where a warring couple might go?
definitions.meaning: The British relationship counselling charity that quarrelling couples visit

explanation.walkthrough: Relate is a UK charity offering marriage and relationship counselling.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate it; the charity is where bickering partners seek help.

clue.text: Copper most unpredictable, one's regularly observed

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: unpredictable letters do not keep a set order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman, most erratic, is under constant watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a tradition or habit that is followed routinely.

clue.text: Outstanding Eastern European housing at college

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the other piece goes in

parts.note: a Serb is a person from Serbia in eastern Europe
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: An exceptional student from the Balkans lives at university.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' when in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Rash ambassador meeting journalist not so often

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title
ed, short for editor, is a stock journalist
less means to a smaller degree, not so much

explanation.surface: An impetuous diplomat meets a reporter less frequently.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless of consequences, reckless.

clue.text: River is immacutely clean, ignoring the source

indicators.note: the source of a river is where it starts, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: spotless, immaculately clean means pure (the clue misspells immaculately)

explanation.surface: A river is spotless, apart from its spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'immacutely' is a misprint for 'immaculately'. PURE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: More advanced figure rose in ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or pulverised, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pattern of a rose is worked into the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior person is older or of higher rank than others.

clue.text: Pursuit of an ace?

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot, and flying is his pursuit or occupation; pursuit also hints at aerial chases

explanation.walkthrough: 'ace' suggests a playing card or tennis serve, but here is a star pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying aircraft is the occupation that an expert pilot follows.
